idiom_name: http crate Request<T>/Response<T> (HeaderMap + generic body); tonic MetadataMap + prost message
implementation_notes: The http crate is the ecosystem's message type: Request<T> and Response<T> are generic over the body, so one head (method/status/version plus HeaderMap, a typed, optimized header container) can carry Vec<u8>, bytes::Bytes, a stream, or an already-deserialized value - the header/body split lives in the type system instead of a base class, which is why hyper, axum and reqwest share it. On the RPC/broker side tonic carries MetadataMap (headers) alongside a prost-generated message (body) and the transport keeps them in one call unit. A serde-annotated struct with an explicit header map is the hand-rolled option when no framework type fits, at the cost of writing the framing yourself.
code_sketch:
let req = Request::builder()
    .method("POST")
    .uri("https://api.example.com/orders")
    .header("content-type", "application/json")
    .header("x-correlation-id", corr)
    .body(Bytes::from(payload))?;          // T = Bytes

let (parts, body) = resp.into_parts();     // head and body separately
let corr_back = parts.headers.get("x-correlation-id");
pitfalls: Request<T>/Response<T> are generic, so changing the body type (Bytes to a stream to a deserialized struct) ripples through every signature; erase it with Box<dyn Body> deliberately, not by default.
The http crate deliberately defines no Body type, so the actual body plumbing lives in hyper/axum and mixing body types from different crate versions is a common compile error after dependency bumps.
HeaderMap holds HeaderName/HeaderValue: converting values to str requires the fallible to_str(), and names built with HeaderName::from_static panic at runtime if the literal is invalid.
